interfaces.name: Web application
interfaces.classification_rationale: Actions are expressed by manipulating presented affordances (List, Board, Gantt, Calendar and other views) of a persistent, navigable representation of workspace state.

provenance.evidence: Documents a first-party web client alongside desktop and mobile.
Product page lists navigable views and workspace surfaces.

interfaces.name: Desktop application
interfaces.classification_rationale: A first-party desktop client renders the same navigable workspace on a distinct surface; the primitive remains affordance manipulation.

provenance.evidence: Documents native desktop apps for Mac, Windows, and Linux.

interfaces.name: Mobile application
interfaces.classification_rationale: First-party mobile clients present a navigable representation of workspace state; actions are expressed by manipulating on-screen affordances.

provenance.evidence: Documents first-party iOS and Android apps.
Provider's App Store listing for the mobile client.

interfaces.name: REST API (v2 / v3)
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes provider-defined operations (Tasks, Chat, Docs, Comments, Views, Time Tracking, webhook management) through structured requests under one base and one auth scheme.

provenance.evidence: API reference exposing named endpoints under api.clickup.com/api/v2 and /v3 with personal token or OAuth auth.
Index of endpoints across Tasks, Chat, Docs, and webhook management sharing the same base and auth.

interfaces.name: Inbound email to task / comment
interfaces.technology: Email submission to a ClickUp-issued address
interfaces.classification_rationale: Sending a message to a unique ClickUp-issued task or List address invokes a create-task or create-comment operation encoded by the address; the primitive is operation invocation by message submission, not natural-language interpretation.

provenance.evidence: Unique addresses per task and List; sending an email creates a task or comment.
Email ClickApp enabling task and comment creation by email.

interfaces.name: Webhooks
interfaces.technology: HTTP callbacks to a subscriber URL
interfaces.classification_rationale: ClickUp initiates the interaction when subscribed events occur and delivers to a consumer-controlled receiver URL, which is event notification rather than consumer-invoked retrieval.

provenance.evidence: Documents subscribing to events and delivery to a receiver.
Create Webhook endpoint monitoring events and posting to a URL.

interfaces.name: MCP Server
interfaces.classification_rationale: The official MCP server exposes semantically described tools that are discoverable and selectable as part of the interaction contract, so discovery and selection structure the contract rather than mere operation invocation.

provenance.evidence: Documents ClickUp's official MCP server for AI assistants.
Lists the supported tools the MCP server advertises for selection.

interfaces.name: ClickUp Brain
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer interacts through natural-language messages the service interprets; task creation, search, and summarization are orchestrated internally and are not exposed as a discovery contract, so it is Conversational rather than Agentic.

provenance.evidence: Brain is chatted with using natural language and asks for clarification.
Describes Brain as a native AI assistant acting across the workspace.
